Sea otters spend most of their lives in the water. To stay warm, they do not rely on a thick layer of fat the way seals do. Instead, they have the thickest fur of any animal. The dense fur traps a layer of air against their skin, which keeps them warm even in cold ocean water.

According to the passage, how do sea otters stay warm in cold water?
items.answer: Their thick fur traps a layer of air against their skin, which keeps them warm.

steps: The question asks for an explicitly stated detail about how sea otters stay warm.
The last two sentences say otters have the thickest fur of any animal and that the dense fur traps a layer of air against their skin.
The passage then states this trapped air keeps them warm even in cold ocean water.
So the answer is that their thick fur traps air against their skin to keep them warm.
